reason: Both re-stack the design sensibly for the tall format and keep the brand intact, but both break the headline so 'fizz' sits alone on its own line, and both crop the circles hard. A sits the product low, which leaves a big gap under the logo. Its CTA is jammed right under the body copy, and the button nearly touches the tan circle in the bottom-left. B moves the whole stack up, so the logo/product/headline spacing is more even and the CTA gets more room above and below. That makes B somewhat more balanced, though the gap between product and headline is still loose.

The two candidates are nearly identical banners, and both are clearly broken. Each crams the full 4-line headline, the body paragraph, a 'Ships late June' note wrapped into a 3-word column, and a block of fine print into one strip. The SOLSTICE wordmark is jammed against the bottom of a small dark logo panel, and 'Limited Summer Release' is stranded below it. The Reserve a Case button is a small pill in the top-right corner, so the CTA is buried. The legal text is illegibly tiny, packed against the right edge and almost as heavy as the body copy. There is no left-to-right hierarchy, just a shrunk copy of the original. The small differences in button and text positions don't make either one better.

Both use the same broken layout. The body copy is much larger than the CTA, so the 'Reserve a Case' button is a tiny, unreadable pill crammed into the right column. The 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow and the legal text are illegible specks, and the right column of fine print is a cramped clump next to the large body text. B's CTA label is slightly more legible, but its orange divider sits almost on top of 'Evenings'. A's eyebrow and rule are reduced to an indistinct dash cluster above the button. Neither is shippable.

A: the header bar no longer spans the full width but is evenly inset, which looks deliberate. The gaps between the eyebrow and headline and between the body and CTA are too large. 'Ships late June' has drifted away from the button and now sits on top of the legal text. B: the header bar is off-centre (flush near the left, a gap on the right), which reads as a bug. The upper stack is tighter, but 'Ships late June' floats alone in a large dead area below the CTA. Neither shrinks the oversized six-line headline.

Both cram the whole poster into a tiny leaderboard. The headline is stacked into three lines on the left, while the body copy and legal text are shrunk to an unreadable micro size, the legal text is about as large as the body copy, and the Solstice logo is too small to see. In A the body copy sits below the dark band, but in B it rides up into the dark strip, so dark text lands on a dark ground. That collision makes B slightly worse.

Both use the same broken 320x50 layout. The legal fine print is a big multi-line block on the far left, as prominent as the headline. The SOLSTICE logo and the product can are specks too small to read, and the 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon is shrunk to an unreadable sliver under the headline, so the sale message is lost. A's left-aligned headline puts the ribbon close to 'longer' in a way that looks almost like a collision, while B's centred headline with the ribbon tucked under it is a little tidier. Otherwise the two are essentially the same.

A and B look pixel-identical, so this is a tie. Both keep the brand, colours, fonts and hierarchy, but share the same flaws: the headline is too big and wraps into five lines with the short line 'little', and 'botanicals' nearly touches the left and right edges. The top margin is tight, there is an uneven empty gap between the headline and the 'Now in four flavours' subline, and the CTA sits close to the bottom edge.

I'd ship B before A, but both still need fixes. A has no consistent left edge: the logo, subtext and flavour pills sit at about x=76 while the headline starts further left at about x=64, so it looks ragged. A's headline also runs to within about 30px of the right edge, its pills sit closer together than the gap below the CTA, and the bottom is dead space. B lines the logo, headline, subtext and pills up on one left margin at about 45px, and its pill gaps are even. Both share the same problems: the CTA floats on its own on the right between the copy and the pills, so the flavour pills come after the button in reading order. The peach circle in the top right is shrunk to a small scrap in the corner, and the yellow circle sits behind the start of the headline.

The two are almost identical. In both, the CTA floats on the right in the gap between the subhead and the pills, sitting so close above the flavour pills that it feels jammed. The headline runs to about 45px from the right edge against a 74px left margin, and the lower half is mostly dead space apart from a clipped peach circle. B edges ahead because its CTA's left edge lines up with the Honey Rosemary pill. A's CTA sits about 10px off that line, so it looks almost aligned but not quite.

Both use the same competent stacked layout: label, headline, body and CTA on a shared left edge, with the bottle and circle at the bottom. In both, the bottle cap sits almost against the Shop Sale button, and the bottle-plus-circle cluster is crowded into the lower-left with only a thin margin at the bottom. A starts its text lower (about 70px top margin against about 38px at the bottom), so the top is unbalanced and the gap between the CTA and the bottle cap is only about 20px. B's top margin (about 30px) is close to its side margins, and it leaves more space between the text lines and above the bottle, so it is very slightly more even.

The two layouts are almost identical. Both crop the cream product circle against the top-left canvas edges, which reads as a clumsy bleed. Both leave a large dead orange area at top right. In both, 'Out now.' is indented about 44px from the headline's left edge, so it is not aligned, and the oversized 'Try It' pill competes with the headline for attention. A is a little worse because its CTA sits only about 48px from the bottom edge, which makes the lower half feel cramped. B moves the text block and button up for a better bottom margin, although the headline then sits a little tight under the circle.

Both break up the badge row: FREE ENTRY is stranded under the date block while ALL AGES and TASTINGS sit above the CTA. Both also jam the date, badges and RSVP button into a cramped lower band, and the centred headline column is off-centre on the canvas. In A, the URL line runs right into the partner-mark placeholder, and the address wraps badly ('Harbour / Rooftop, Pier 9'). B wraps the address more cleanly and keeps the URL clear of the placeholder, but its headline column is shifted even further left of centre.

The two layouts are the same except for how the quote wraps. Both share these flaws: the attribution is indented (x≈49) instead of lining up with the quote's left edge (x≈27), it sits cramped right under the quote's last line, it touches the top of the background circle, and the can floats in the middle of a big empty circle. A keeps 'a glass' together and its line lengths are more even. B's first line is long ('in a') and the rag is uneven ('glass: bright, a' is short). Both leave 'a' dangling at the end of a line.

Both use the same weak leaderboard layout. The logo is jammed against the headline at the left edge, and the SAVE 15% badge floats on its own above the body copy. The coffee bag is shrunk to a tiny sliver that is cut off at the right edge, so the key product image is lost, and the small body copy has weak contrast. A's badge sticks out past the right edge of the body copy and its button is shorter. B's wider button is a slightly stronger CTA and its badge lines up a little better, but the difference is marginal.

The two candidates use almost the same layout and share the same flaws. The shoe circle is shrunk and pushed down into the bottom-left corner, so it no longer reads as the hero. 'Full review inside.' floats on its own to the right of the circle with nothing to anchor it, and the bottom-right area is left empty. The only difference is spacing: A's headline sits too low, so the gap above it to the logo row is loose while the circle crowds it from below (about 45px). B puts the headline higher, which spaces the logo, headline and circle a little more evenly.

A and B look pixel-identical. Both have the same flaws. The three price cards are shrunk to tiny chips: the MONTHLY/YEARLY/FAMILY labels and the 'per month'/'per year' text can't be read, and the cards are reordered to 6/80/48, which breaks the original sequence. The subhead and legal copy are jammed into a cramped stack against the right edge, and the fine print is about as large as the subhead. The logo is undersized and floats on its own at the left.

Both rebuild the square as a proper vertical stack with the brand intact, but both break the headline so 'fizz' sits alone on its own line, and both shrink the peach circle into a stub in the corner. A spaces things better: the can sits higher, there is room between the can and the headline, and the CTA has a comfortable bottom margin. B pushes the can down, which leaves a dead gap under the logo, and it jams the CTA against the body copy (about 12px apart) so the bottom feels cramped.

Both use the same broken leaderboard approach. Each crams six columns into 90px: the SOLSTICE wordmark is tiny and sits low in the dark tile, the 4-line headline competes with the body copy, 'Ships late June' wraps into a one-word-per-line stack, and the fine print is illegible and as prominent as the CTA, which is a small button pushed into the corner. A is marginally worse because 'Ships late June' is jammed between the body copy and the legal text with almost no gutter. B gives it slightly more room, but B's headline runs almost into the body column.

Both use the same broken layout. The body copy is set larger than the CTA, the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow has shrunk to an unreadable hairline under the headline, the legal text is microscopic, and the CTA button is a tiny pill wedged in the lower right. That buries the action and flips the hierarchy. A's button and label are slightly bigger and more readable; B's 'Reserve a Case' is squeezed into an even smaller, more cramped pill.

A: the dark header bar is shifted left and stops about 40px short of the right edge, so the brand bar visibly misaligns with the centred content. There is also a large dead gap between the eyebrow and the headline, and 'Ships late June' floats about 90px below the CTA, cut off from its button. B: the header is inset on both sides, so it doesn't bleed to the edges, but at least it is symmetric. Its vertical spacing is overstretched, with big uneven gaps around the body copy and CTA, and 'Ships late June' drifts down beside the legal text instead of sitting with the button. Both keep a legible headline wrap, but B's centred header makes it slightly less broken.

Both cram the full portrait layout into a tiny banner. In each, the headline wraps to three lines on the left, while the body copy and legal text on the right are shrunk past legibility. The legal text is nearly as large as the body copy, so the hierarchy is flat. Neither shows the SOLSTICE sun logo clearly, and the CTA pill is tiny and buried. B is marginally better because it keeps the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow and arranges the copy column a little more cleanly, but it has the same unreadable-text and cramming failures as A.

Both 320x50 banners make the same core mistakes. The legal fine print sits on the left, wrapped into 4 lines and nearly as prominent as the headline, so the hierarchy is wrong. The 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon has shrunk to an illegible sliver under the headline, and the logo and can are reduced to tiny marks. A leaves a clean gutter between the headline and the 'Claim the Deal' button. In B the button is jammed almost against the end of the headline and the ribbon is pushed further right, which makes B more cramped.

A and B look pixel-identical, so neither is the better resize. Both have the same flaws: the headline is set so large that 'botanicals' runs almost edge to edge with no side margin. It also breaks into five ragged lines, leaving 'little' alone on its own line. The subline sits after an oversized, uneven gap below the headline, and the CTA is pushed close to the bottom edge, so the vertical spacing feels uneven rather than planned. Brand colours, fonts and hierarchy do survive.

A holds one clean left edge (x≈45) for wordmark, headline, subline and pills, and its margins are even. Its flaws: the CTA floats on the right, under and out of line with the headline's right edge, and the flavour pills sit below the CTA, which breaks the reading order. B has a ragged left edge: the headline starts at x≈65 while the wordmark, subline and pills start at x≈76. Its headline runs almost to the right canvas edge, the subline is jammed under the headline, and it has the same pills-below-CTA ordering problem, so it is the weaker of the two.

Both use the same layout. The CTA sits awkwardly between the subhead and the flavour pills, which breaks the original left-text/right-CTA split and leaves a dead band on the right with only a small stray peach circle. 'SOLSTICE' and the headline also sit on the yellow circles. A's CTA lines up with the left edge of the Honey Rosemary pill (x≈460). B's CTA is pushed about 10px right, where it lines up with neither the pill nor the end of the headline, so it looks arbitrary.

The two layouts are almost the same. In both, the bottle is pushed into the bottom-right corner with only about 35px left below it, and the circle is cropped off the bottom-left. That makes the lower half feel crowded, and the bottle sits off the text's left edge with nothing to line it up to. B moves the whole text block about 30px lower, which squeezes the gaps between the body copy and the button and between the button and the bottle cap (about 20px). A spaces things a little more evenly, with a cleaner top margin and more room above the bottle.

The two layouts are almost identical and share the same flaws. The product circle is cropped hard into the top-left corner and leaves a big empty orange area to its right. 'Out now.' is indented and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge. The 'Try It' pill is oversized and pulls attention from the headline. A crowds the headline right under the circle and leaves extra empty space at the bottom. B spaces the elements more evenly down the canvas, though its button sits a little close to the bottom edge.

Both split the three chips: FREE ENTRY is stranded under the date block while ALL AGES and TASTINGS sit apart above the RSVP button. Both also wedge 'Saturday 21 June' tightly under the subtitle and leave the central column off-centre. A is the cleaner of the two. B's 'Reserve a spot' line almost touches the partner-mark box, and its venue line breaks awkwardly as 'Harbour / Rooftop, Pier 9'.

The two layouts are almost identical, and both share the same flaws. The 'THE GROVE TASTING TEAM' attribution is indented from the quote's left edge and sits tight under it, right on the top edge of the circle. The circle and the can float in the middle instead of being anchored to the corner, which leaves the can small. The logo sits inside the circle with no clear spacing. The only difference is how the quote wraps: A's rag is uneven (a long first line, then a short 'glass: bright, a'), while B's line lengths are more balanced, so B is slightly better.

The two are nearly identical and both have the same problems. The logo is crammed against the top-left edge, clipped and touching the headline. The coffee bag is shrunk to an unreadable sliver jammed against the right edge, so the hero product is lost. The two-line body copy is tiny at 90 px tall, and the SAVE 15% pill floats on its own above the copy. A spreads the CTA farther right, leaving a wide gap. B pulls the body copy, badge and CTA into a slightly tighter group, but this is only marginally better.

The two layouts are almost the same. In both, the shoe circle is shrunk into the lower-left corner, so the hero image loses impact. The 'Full review inside.' line floats on its own to the right of the circle, small and lined up with nothing. There is also dead space under and around the circle. The difference is the headline. In A it sits with even gaps above and below (about 75px to the logo row and 70px to the circle). In B it drops lower, leaving a big gap under the logo and squeezing the headline against the circle, so A's vertical rhythm is slightly better.

The two candidates look pixel-identical. Both shrink the plan cards into tiny chips. The MONTHLY/YEARLY/FAMILY labels and per-month captions can't be read, and the cards are reordered to 6, 80, 48, so the highlighted yearly plan loses its central spot. The subhead and legal fine print are squeezed into a cramped right-edge column that touches the canvas edge, with fine print almost as large as the subhead.

A keeps the original's stack and the CTA stays clear of the olive circle, but everything is pushed toward the top, which leaves dead space under the button, and the headline wraps to an orphaned 'fizz'. B has the same orphaned 'fizz', and it also pushes the 'Find a Store' button into the olive circle, which looks like an accidental collision. B also crowds the CTA tight under the headline while leaving a large gap between the logo and the bag.

A and B are practically the same layout, with only pixel-level shifts in the dark logo panel and the body text, so they share the same flaws. The dark logo block touches the top edge but floats off the left edge and takes up a large share of the canvas. The orange divider sits stranded above the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow, and that eyebrow now sits under the logo panel instead of introducing the headline, which breaks the reading order. On the right, the body copy is cramped against the right edge, the legal text is too small to read, and the CTA is crowded between them.

Both use the same weak layout. The bottle is shrunk to a tiny afterthought, the supporting copy is a cramped four-line ragged block jammed against the CTA with a bokeh dot over 'sunset', the fine print is illegibly small, and the left side is mostly dead space. A also crowds its headline against the right edge with a decorative circle hitting 'last', and its bottle nearly touches the bottom edge; B's tighter headline wrap and higher bottle are slightly cleaner, though 'day last' sits close to the button.

The two layouts are almost identical, and both share the same flaws. The SOLSTICE wordmark floats off-centre and doesn't line up with the left-aligned headline. The badges and CTA are pushed to the right while the headline and body copy sit on the left, so the column edges are ragged. The two badges nearly touch, and the wordmark is jammed under the circle. A edges ahead on vertical balance, with roughly equal top and bottom margins; B pushes the circle close to the top edge and leaves a larger empty band at the bottom.

The two are almost identical: the headline is crammed against a narrow right column, with the period after 'sunshine.' nearly touching the CTA. The subcopy breaks into four centered lines and ends on an orphaned 'flavours.'. In A the subcopy and button sit together and are centered vertically against the headline. In B a looser gap pushes the button lower, closer to the bottom edge and out of line with the headline, so A is marginally better.

Both use the same layout: the headline is stacked on top and the subhead and CTA share one row at the bottom. That row sits close to the bottom edge, and the italic 'Now in four flavours' is very small. A breaks the headline cleanly ('Bubbles, / botanicals / and a little / sunshine.'). B breaks it as 'botanicals and / a little', which makes the lines ragged and pushes the headline nearer the side edges. B's subhead also sits tighter to the left edge.

Both use the same 5-line headline. It runs almost to the side edges, wraps with 'little' alone on its own line, and the subtitle sits jammed right under 'sunshine.'. A anchors the CTA near the bottom edge, so the canvas fills evenly, but there is a loose ~100px gap that detaches the button from its copy and only a thin bottom margin. B keeps the CTA grouped with the copy, but the whole block is pushed up with about 45px at the top and about 110px of dead orange at the bottom, so it looks top-heavy rather than centred like the original.

Both candidates use almost the same top-to-bottom stack. In both, the headline runs nearly to the right edge, the CTA button is also close to the edges, the pills have mismatched widths and come in reverse order (Honey Rosemary first), and the bottom-right circle is clipped behind the fine print. A keeps the subhead closer to the headline and the spacing a little more even. B leaves a large empty gap between the headline and the subhead, then crowds the CTA against the pills.

Both copy the leaderboard's single row onto a taller canvas without redesigning it. The bottle circle is jammed into the top-left corner with a stray clipped circle behind it, and the headline sits flush against it. A pushes the NEW pill and Try It button down to the bottom edge, which leaves a dead orange band in the middle and separates them from the headline. B keeps the buttons close under the headline but crams everything into the top 60% and leaves the bottom third empty, which is lopsided. A's weight is spread a little better, so it edges out B.

Both have the same broken leaderboard layout. The RSVP CTA is shrunk into a pill that looks like the FREE ENTRY, ALL AGES and TASTINGS badges, so the call to action no longer stands out. The time and venue line is cut off from its date and stranded at the far right. A red placeholder chip for a missing asset is left in the badge row, and the left-column copy is tiny and cramped. B is slightly worse because its pills overlap each other (FREE ENTRY, ALL AGES and TASTINGS collide), and its can graphic is more crushed and awkwardly placed. A's pills sit side by side with small gaps.

The two candidates are effectively the same image; the only difference is that B's text sits a pixel or two further right. Both share the same flaws: the wordmark logo has moved from its bottom-left anchor to float in mid-canvas between the quote and the can, where it reads as a stray element. The can's 'SOLSTICE' label is too small to read, the circle is fully enclosed instead of bleeding off the edge as in the original, and the quote mark and text are crowded toward the left edge and the top and bottom.

A: the attribution floats about 60px below the quote, so it no longer reads as part of it. It is also indented to x≈18 while the quote starts at x≈10, and the logo row sits on the purple circle and is jammed against the bottom edge. B keeps the attribution with the quote, but the gap is too tight and the same left-edge misalignment remains. The quote mark is offset further right than the text, there is a dead band above the quote, and the logo is still cramped onto the circle near the bottom.

The two layouts are almost identical. Both drop the 'Quiet Hours' book cover, which was the hero image, so the original loses its key visual. Both also shrink the Inkwell & Lantern logo to an illegible speck in the top-left corner and leave the fine print tiny. B's logo looks clipped or garbled ('NOWELL & ANTERN'), which damages the brand mark more than A's. B wraps the body copy more cleanly ('Tea and toast all night' stays on one line), while A breaks it awkwardly before 'and'. I gave A the edge because the logo matters more than the line break.

A pushes the stack too low: the 'Find a Store' button runs into the olive circle (an unintended collision), it's squeezed under the headline, there's dead space between the logo and the bag, and the bottom margin is cramped. B keeps the content higher so the CTA clears the olive circle, and its spacing is more even. Both break the headline onto two lines with 'fizz' left alone on the second, and B leaves a fairly empty bottom area that only the circle fills.

The two layouts are nearly identical, and both have the same problems. The dark logo panel touches the top edge of the canvas but sits inset from the left. The orange divider is stranded on its own above 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE', and that tagline is placed under the logo instead of leading into the headline, which breaks the reading order. The right column is cramped: the legal text is around 5px, unreadable, and jammed under the CTA, and the button nearly touches the right edge. B wins narrowly because its body copy starts lower, so it isn't crowding the top edge as much as in A, and it sits better above the button.

Both candidates use the same broken banner layout. The bottle is shrunk to a tiny, trivial icon, and the four-line body copy is jammed against the left edge of the CTA. The legal text is unreadably small and pushed against the right edge, and decorative dots sit on the body copy. The headline is jammed directly on top of the CTA in both. B wins narrowly because its headline wrap ('Make the / longest day last') matches the original. A's 'Make the longest / day last' leaves an awkward short last line, and B's bottle is slightly smaller still.

The two layouts are almost identical and share the same flaws. The SOLSTICE wordmark floats right of centre while the headline and body copy are left-aligned. The badges and CTA hug the right edge, so they don't line up with the copy. The two badges almost touch each other and are crammed right under the body copy, which breaks the grid. A sits too high, with a thin top margin and dead space at the bottom; B moves the whole stack down for slightly better vertical balance, but its circle presses closer to the wordmark.

The two layouts are nearly identical. In both, the headline runs almost the full width, and its final period nearly touches the left edge of the CTA button. The supporting copy is squeezed into a narrow 4-line column with awkward breaks ('Now in four / flavours.'), and the right-hand block looks cramped against the edge. A's right column is placed worse: the copy starts high and the button sits close to the bottom edge, so the group doesn't line up with the headline's vertical centre. B's right group is slightly more centred against the headline, which gives it marginally better balance.

Both use the same structure: the headline is pushed high with a tight top margin, and the subline and CTA are squeezed into one bottom row. The subline is tiny there and the CTA pill sits close to the right and bottom edges, which leaves the layout top-heavy and the centred axis of the original broken. A's headline breaks awkwardly ('botanicals and / a little / sunshine.'), leaving a ragged two-word line. B breaks it more naturally ('botanicals / and a little / sunshine.') and its CTA is slightly larger, so B is marginally better.

Both use the same oversized 5-line headline. It has awkward breaks ('and a' / 'little'), and 'botanicals' runs within about 30px of both side edges. In A, the subline and CTA are packed tightly under the headline, which leaves a dead orange band of about 110px at the bottom and makes the layout top-heavy. B fills the height better by anchoring the CTA near the bottom, but that splits the CTA from its subline with a large gap, and the CTA sits tighter to the bottom edge than the headline does to the top.

Both use the same stacked skyscraper layout, and both share the same flaws. The flavour pills have different widths and ragged centring, so they don't line up with the left text edge, and their order is reversed from the original. The CTA and the headline run almost to the canvas edges, and the fine print is tiny. A is slightly worse: there is a large dead gap between the headline and the body copy, and the body copy breaks awkwardly as "one / long season". B keeps the headline and body copy together as a group and wraps the line more cleanly.

A packs the bottle, headline and buttons into the top 60% and leaves a dead orange band across the bottom. Its bottle circle is jammed into the top-left corner with the bottle cap cropped, and a stray faint circle sits behind it. B spreads the weight better by moving NEW/Try It to the bottom right, but that leaves a large empty middle, disconnects the CTA from the headline and puts the buttons close to the bottom edge. B keeps the same cramped bottle in the corner, and neither candidate really rearranges the layout for the taller shape.

I'd ship neither. They're almost the same scattered banner, and A is slightly less cramped. In both, the subhead and URL sit in the left column ahead of the headline, so the reading order is jumbled. The RSVP CTA has shrunk to a pill the same size as the Free Entry, All Ages and Tastings tags, so it no longer stands out, and the venue copy is pushed to the far right, away from the date. The broken missing-asset fragment is still showing. B's tag pills are larger and jammed edge to edge, and the date is tighter under the headline. A spaces both a little better.

The two candidates are almost pixel-identical. Each has a sensible left-to-right banner flow, with the quote mark and quote on the left and the can on the right, but both share the same flaws. The brand logo floats in the middle gap with no alignment to anything, so it looks like an orphan. The can is shrunk so far that the SOLSTICE label is unreadable, and its backdrop circle is now a small, fully contained disc instead of a large cropped shape. The quote block is also crammed against the left edge, which leaves the right half underused.

A keeps the attribution directly under the quote, which preserves the grouping, but the attribution is indented and doesn't line up with the quote's left edge at x≈10. In both, the logo strip sits jammed against the bottom of the can, inside the purple circle. B pushes 'THE ULTRA TASTING TEAM' about 100px below the quote, so it floats on its own in dead space, which breaks proximity and reading order. B has the same logo/can crowding and misaligned attribution as A.

Both use the same banner layout. Both drop 'The Quiet Hours' book cover, which was the original's hero image, and shrink the Inkwell & Lantern logo to an illegible speck in the top-left corner. Both also leave a large empty band on the card's left side and set the fine print too small to read. A's logo text looks clipped ('NKWELL & ANTERN'), which damages the brand. B's logo looks intact but is even smaller, and its body copy has an awkward 'Tea / and toast' line break. B edges ahead only because its logo appears whole.

Both candidates are practically the same layout. The only difference is that B's 'Find a Store' button sits a few pixels further right. Both share the same flaws. The peach circle sits behind the body copy, and the green circle's top is cut off by the canvas edge. The 'SOLSTICE' label on the can is too small to read. The headline is jammed between the product and the copy row, and the small body copy has to compete with the CTA on one cramped bottom line.

Both resizes are almost the same and share the same faults. The dark header band has become a large empty black block in the top-left, and the logo is shrunk to an illegible dot in its corner, so the brand mark is lost. The headline is crammed into a narrow right column, and the body copy, a tiny CTA, 'Ships late June' and the fine print are packed into the bottom with no breathing room. The CTA is no longer prominent and the divider is stranded. The only difference is that B's button text fills its pill edge to edge while A's keeps a little padding, which makes A marginally cleaner.

Both put the tiny, barely legible 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow below the headline instead of above it, shrink the logo to a speck, and drop the orange divider below the legal text where it means nothing. A is worse on spacing: big dead gaps around the stranded eyebrow and a CTA pushed low with the legal copy jammed right under it. B spaces headline, body, CTA and legal more evenly, and the button has room around it.

The two layouts are almost the same, and both share the same flaws. The bottom row is crammed: '25% off on June 21.' is squeezed against the CTA. The legal text is almost as large as the subcopy and sits tight against the right edge. The phone nearly touches the top and bottom edges, and the decorative circle crowds the sun logo in the top-left corner. A's headline is set larger and pushed up toward the top edge ('Make the / longest day last' leaves a short first line), and it almost runs into the CTA. B keeps the original line break, gives the headline a little more room at the top, and sits slightly calmer overall.

The two layouts are almost the same. The only difference is that the tilted FREE DELIVERY badge sits a few pixels higher in B. Both have the same problems. The CTA 'Find It Near You' is pushed to the top-right corner, above and beside the headline, so the reading order is wrong. The CTA, the two pills and the tilted badge are stacked in one column, so the button reads as just another badge. The body copy is shrunk to tiny text wedged into the bottom-right corner, right against the canvas edge. The product circle is cut off at the bottom edge, leaving the left half cramped against empty gaps.

The two layouts are almost the same, and both have the same main flaws. The GROVE wordmark is centred but the headline and body copy are left-aligned, while the badges and CTA are pushed right, so the left edge doesn't line up. The two badges nearly touch each other, the badges sit too close under the body copy, and the badges and CTA run right up to the right edge. A is worse because its bottom group is lower and more cramped, with only about 38px below the CTA, and it has a large gap above the circle. B moves everything up, which leaves the spacing at the top and bottom slightly more even.

The two layouts are almost the same: the headline is reflowed to 4 lines with a good size step, and the CTA is kept, but in both the LIMITED badge sits about 40px from the left edge, so it looks pushed out of the centred axis and crowds the edge. The CTA is also tight under the headline while a large dead orange band fills the bottom. A sits higher, with about 60px at the top and about 170px of empty space at the bottom, so it is more top-heavy; B's block is a little lower and better balanced vertically, which makes it marginally better.

Both use the same broken leaderboard layout. The dark CTA is the oversized first element on the left, so the reading order runs backwards. SOLSTICE sits below the headline when it should come first, the flavour pills appear in reverse order, the body copy is squeezed into a cramped two-line block, and the fine print floats alone in a large dead zone on the right. A is worse because SOLSTICE is jammed directly under the headline and nearly touches it; B gives it slightly more breathing room.

The two layouts are nearly identical, and both share the same main flaw. The 'Shop Flavours' CTA is jammed right after the subtitle with almost no gap, so it reads as an add-on to that line instead of a separate action. The legal line is also tiny and the pills sit loosely below. In B the logo and headline are pushed lower, which crowds the subtitle, pills and legal line together at the bottom and leaves dead space at the top. A spaces the content more evenly from top to bottom, so it has a slight edge.

Both use the same broken layout. 'WEEKEND ONLY' sits far above '20% off', and the subcopy floats above and to the right of the headline, so the reading order is jumbled. The CTA drifts in its own middle column away from the headline, and the legal line is unreadably tiny under the product circle. A's middle column hugs the headline unevenly, while B's subcopy and button sit slightly more centred in the gap, so B is marginally better balanced.

The two candidates are essentially pixel-identical, so I've scored them the same. Both use a sensible left-to-right banner order (headline, copy, can, CTA), but they share the same flaws. The 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow sits almost against the top edge. The '20% off' headline nearly touches the 'Every mixed case' copy, and that copy is about as big as the headline, so the two compete for attention. The can is shrunk to a small sticker, which makes its 'SOLSTICE' label unreadable. The legal line under the button is too small and faint to read.

A and B are almost pixel-identical. Both squeeze the subhead 'Every mixed case.' into a cramped three-line wrap next to the Shop Sale button, and both shrink the legal line to illegible micro-text jammed under the CTA. In both, the shoe sits off-centre in the bottom-left of the peach circle, leaving the top of the circle empty. Everything is pushed into a crowded bottom strip. The only difference is that B's circle and shoe sit a few pixels lower, which changes nothing.

Both pull the 'Out now.' subline away from the headline and put it next to the button, which breaks the grouping. Both also stack the CTA directly under the product circle, leaving the left half and the bottom empty. In A the 'Try It' button overlaps the bottom of the cream circle and 'Out now.' is jammed against the button. B has the same structure, but the button only just touches the circle and 'Out now.' has a little breathing room, so it is slightly cleaner.

A: the two-column layout works, but the logo has shrunk to a tiny dot beside the eyebrow, so the brand mark is lost. The bag is pushed into the bottom-left corner, sitting off the headline's left edge and away from the circle, and the legal line is unreadably small. B has the same tiny logo and legal line, plus a worse problem: the headline is shifted right until 'better cup' almost touches the '03' numeral, which reads as a collision between the columns. The logo, the eyebrow and the circle/bag also sit on three different left edges, so the left column looks ragged.

Both use the same rearranged layout: the headline at top left and the shoe under it. The empty upper right and the strong bottom-heavy weight on the right look a bit unresolved in both. In A, the subcopy wraps with an orphaned 'Thursday.' line, but the LIMITED badge sits close to the CTA as one group with a sensible right margin. In B, the subcopy wraps more evenly, but the badge is pushed against the right edge (about 27px margin) and drifts away from the button, while the CTA's bottom edge sits close to the canvas bottom.

Both use the same weak layout. The headline is small and isolated top-left above a large empty area on the left-middle. The shoe sits off to the right. The LIMITED badge has drifted to the far bottom-right, away from the headline it belongs with, and the bottom row reads as three disconnected fragments. A keeps symmetric margins of about 75px on each side, so the copy and badge frame the canvas evenly. B pushes the headline and copy to about 25px from the left edge while the badge stays about 77px from the right, which leaves the layout lopsided and cramped against the left edge.

Both make the same structural mistakes. The subhead is squeezed into a narrow left column and wraps to 7 lines at nearly headline size, so it competes with the headline. The YEARLY card has shrunk below the other two, which kills the emphasis it had in the original. The legal text is unreadably tiny. The left column is also cramped against the canvas edge. A puts the CTA level with the top of the cards, which leaves it floating with dead space below. B centres the CTA beside the card row, which groups it a bit better, but B's subhead almost touches the MONTHLY card.

The two are almost pixel-identical. Both use a reasonable banner layout: logo and headline on the left, product can on the green circle at right. Both share the same flaws: the 'fizz' end of the headline runs into the green circle, the body copy is tiny (~9px) and sits on the yellow circle, and the bottom row is cramped against the bottom edge. The CTA in A is a few pixels tighter to the right edge than in B, a negligible difference.

The two candidates look almost identical and both have the same faults. The dark header became a large, empty black block in the top-left, and the Q logo inside it shrank to an unreadable dot, so the brand is effectively lost. The 8-line headline is crammed into the right column. Body copy, the very small 'Reserve a Case' pill and the legal line are squeezed into the bottom band, the CTA sits too low and lacks prominence, and the left block is unbalanced dead weight. I can't see any meaningful difference between A and B.

Both have the same structural flaws. The 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow has dropped below the headline and is too small to read, the orange divider has drifted under the legal text where it means nothing, the SOLSTICE wordmark is barely visible, and 'Small-Batch' nearly touches the canvas edges. A keeps the spacing fairly even between the headline, body, CTA and legal text. B leaves large dead gaps around the eyebrow and body copy, then jams the legal text right under the 'Reserve a Case' button, so it looks unplanned.

Both share the same flaws: the 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon runs off the left edge and is cut off, the top-left decorative circles look like leftover fragments, the phone almost touches the bottom edge, and the four-line legal text on the far right is jammed against the edge and as heavy as the '25% off' line. A breaks the headline in a balanced way that matches the original ('Make the longest / day last') and leaves a little gap above the CTA. B's break ('Make the / longest day last') gives an uneven rag, and its long second line almost touches the 'Claim the Deal' button.

A and B use almost the same layout, and both have the same problems. The 'Find It Near You' CTA sits at the top right above the headline, which breaks the reading order. It is stacked in one column with the three badges, so it reads as just another pill. The body copy is pushed into the bottom-right corner below the badges at a tiny size, and the product circle is cramped into the bottom left. The only difference is that B's FREE DELIVERY badge is tilted a bit more and sits a little lower, which makes no meaningful difference.

The two candidates use almost the same layout, and both share the same faults. The centred GROVE wordmark sits over a left-aligned headline and body copy, while the badges and CTA are pushed to the right edge, so the elements have no common alignment axis. The BACK BY DEMAND and SUMMER ONLY pills nearly touch each other and are crammed right under the body copy. B moves the whole stack lower, which leaves a thinner bottom margin under the CTA (about 38px against about 53px) and a tighter gap between the copy and the badges, so A is slightly better balanced.

The two layouts are nearly identical. In both, the headline wraps into four lines with an awkward 'and a little / sunshine.' break, and the CTA pill is oversized, so it competes with the headline. The LIMITED badge plus button cluster also sits slightly left of centre, with the badge close to the left edge. A edges ahead because its block is placed a little lower, closer to the original's vertical balance. B sits higher and leaves a larger empty band at the bottom (~170px), which makes it more top-heavy.

Both put the oversized 'Shop Flavours' CTA hard against the left canvas edge, before the brand and headline, so the reading order runs backwards. Both reverse the flavour pills, squeeze the subhead into a cramped two-line wrap beside them, and float tiny, unreadable legal text in a dead right half. B is worse because the SOLSTICE wordmark collides with the headline descenders and the pills are jammed right under it, while A at least keeps a small gap between the headline, wordmark and pills.

The two layouts are almost the same, and both share the same flaws. In each, the Shop Flavours CTA is jammed right beside the subtitle with a tight gutter and sits on top of the decorative circle, and the legal line is too small to read. A spaces its rows more evenly. In B, the GLACIER wordmark is pushed close to the top edge, which leaves an uneven gap between the logo and the headline compared with the rest of the stack.

The two layouts are almost the same, and both have the same faults. 'WEEKEND ONLY' sits far above '20% off', with a big empty gap between them. The body copy and the Shop Sale button form a separate middle column that is out of line with the headline, so the headline, copy and button don't read as one group. The legal line is shrunk to an unreadable size and left floating under the product circle. The only difference is that B's middle column sits slightly closer to the headline (x≈256 vs 293); that doesn't fix the scattered grouping in either.

The two leaderboards are effectively identical: '20% off' sits on the left, the three-line body copy next to it, the product in a peach circle, and the Shop Sale button on the right. Both share the same flaws. The body copy is set almost as large as the headline, so the two compete for attention. The can is shrunk to a tiny graphic, its label unreadable and its circle sitting on the bottom edge. 'WEEKEND ONLY' is jammed against the top edge, and the 'Ends Sunday' legal line is too small to read at this size.

The two candidates are practically identical. In both, the shoe sits awkwardly off-centre at the lower-left edge of the big circle, leaving a large empty area of peach above it. The subhead 'Every mixed case.' is squeezed into a three-line orphaned stack next to the button. The legal line under 'Shop Sale' is too small to read and sits right against the bottom edge. The shoe in B is only slightly taller and shaped a little differently, which is not enough to separate them.

Both use the same weak layout. The headline sits alone on the left, and the product circle, CTA button and 'Out now.' are stacked into a tight cluster on the right. That leaves a large empty orange area in the middle, and the subline is separated from the headline it belonged to in the original. In A, the button nearly touches the bottom of the circle but there is still a small gap, and 'Out now.' has some breathing room. In B, the button runs right into the circle and 'Out now.' is jammed against the right end of the button with almost no gap, so its cluster is more cramped and looks like a collision.

A: the headline 'better cup' runs right up against the '03' numeral, leaving almost no gutter, so the two columns crowd together. The logo is shrunk to a tiny isolated dot in the far-left margin, and the legal line is illegibly small. B has the same tiny logo and microscopic legal text and a slightly squeezed bag, but it moves the headline left for a clean gutter and puts the logo next to the eyebrow, so the brand, headline, steps and CTA read in a clear order.

The two layouts are almost the same. Both have the same weak structure: the subcopy and CTA column starts at x≈357 and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge, there is a large dead area at the top right, and the pink LIMITED badge sits beside the CTA and competes with it instead of staying a small tag. A breaks the subcopy as 'Draw / closes Thursday.', which is cleaner, but its badge floats off on its own near the right edge. B leaves 'Thursday.' orphaned on the second line and crowds the button up under the copy, though its badge sits closer to the CTA. The orphan in B is the bigger flaw, so A edges it.

The two layouts are almost the same. Each has the headline at top-left, the shoe on the right and a bottom row with the subline, CTA and LIMITED badge. That leaves a large empty block on the left-middle, and the LIMITED badge sits far from the headline it belonged to, beside the CTA. A has uneven margins (about 26px on the left, about 76px on the right), and its shoe floats in the middle with no anchor. B uses matching side margins of about 76px and a larger shoe that is better grounded. Its bottom row is slightly tight under the shoe, and it still has the same dead space and scattered badge.

The two layouts are nearly identical and share the same faults. The subtitle is squeezed into a narrow left column with one or two words per line, and its type is larger than the card copy. The featured YEARLY card has been shrunk smaller than the other two cards, which flips the original hierarchy. The legal text is illegibly tiny. A centres its CTA on the card row, which looks a little more deliberate. B top-aligns its CTA with the cards, leaving a loose gap above the floating legal text.

The two banners are almost identical. In both, the headline breaks badly onto two lines, leaving 'fizz' as an orphan word. The legal text squeezed under the CTA is a few pixels tall and can't be read. The SOLSTICE can is shrunk to a speck, and the logo, can, headline and CTA sit in a cramped row of separate pieces. B adds decorative circles that crowd in behind the logo and can, so A is marginally cleaner.

Both have the same broken composition. The GLACIER wordmark floats alone at top centre-right, above an empty quadrant. The headline and body are indented to x≈255, while the badges and the CTA sit on different, arbitrary left edges, so nothing shares an axis and the left side below the circle is dead space. In A the body copy is jammed against the badge row. B's vertical gaps are slightly more even, so B is marginally better.

Candidate A has a sensible left-to-right banner order. Its flaws: the SOLSTICE wordmark floats off-axis above and left of the headline, and the 'Summer Only' badge is split off to the right while 'Back by Demand' is stacked over the CTA, leaving the two badges ungrouped and the far right dead. The body copy is also tiny. Candidate B has the same split badges and dead right side, plus worse problems: SOLSTICE butts straight into the headline so it reads 'SOLSTICECucumber', the phone is jammed against the top and bottom edges, and there is a big empty gap between the phone and the text.

Both just shrink the centered vertical stack into the wide banner instead of rearranging it left to right, which leaves large empty side areas. The CTA sits only about 12px above the bottom edge in both. A's bigger headline crowds the top edge, and its subline is jammed between headline and CTA. B's slightly smaller headline gives the stack a little more breathing room, though the tiny subline is borderline readable in both.

Both banners use the same cramped strip layout. The product can is shrunk to a meaningless speck, and the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow floats above the button, cut off from the '20% off' headline it belongs to. The low-contrast legal text is too small to read at 50px. A is slightly worse: its legal block butts right against the Shop Sale button with almost no gap, and its can is even tinier and stranded between the body copy and the button. B leaves a little breathing room around the button and wraps the legal text more cleanly.

The two are almost pixel-identical, so neither is the better resize. Both share the same flaws. The lilac circle moved from behind the product to behind the headline, which weakens the link between the circle and the product. '20% off' runs almost to the right edge. The CTA is jammed tight under the subhead. The product floats in a large empty middle area. 'Ends Sunday' fine print is oversized and sits low near the bottom edge.

A: 'Every mixed case.' sits right up against '20% off' with almost no gap, which reads as a collision. The product is tiny and its circle is cramped against the CTA, and the legal text floats alone at the far right. B: the subcopy has a proper gutter and the circle fits cleanly, but the legal line butts right up against the circle and leaves a dead strip on the right. In both, the product is shrunk to an icon and the 3-line subcopy wraps awkwardly.

Both are nearly the same skyscraper restack, with the headline, then the CTA, then the product, then the footer. In both, the full-width Shop Sale button sits only about 10px from the canvas edges and almost touches the lilac circle. A also wraps the subhead badly, leaving 'case.' alone on its own line, and it bunches content up top while leaving a dead gap of about 80px between the can and the footer. B's 'Every / mixed case.' wrap reads better and its vertical rhythm is more even. However, the gap above B's CTA is a bit large, and its can sits close to the footer.

A and B are almost pixel-identical. B moves the NEW pill and the Try It button up a few pixels, which gives a slightly larger bottom margin but changes nothing important. Both share the same flaws: the bottle's cap nearly touches the top edge, and its cream circle bleeds off the top-left corner. The top-right is a large empty area, and the left-aligned headline sits against right-aligned buttons with no shared axis. The NEW badge is almost as big as the CTA, so the two compete as focal points.

The two candidates are almost identical. Both stack the headline, the phone in its circle, the rotated ONLINE ONLY pill, the Try It button and the subline from top to bottom, which suits a tall skyscraper. Both share the same flaws. The subline 'New botanical sparkling, out now.' drops below the CTA, which breaks the original reading order. It is also set as large as the button label, so the hierarchy is weak. The left-aligned copy clashes with the centred badge and button. The badge and button nearly touch the side edges and are jammed together. The only visible difference is the phone: in B it pokes slightly above the circle, like the original, while in A it sits a touch lower inside the circle. That is not enough to separate them.

I can't see any difference between A and B, so they share the same flaws. The badge pills are blown up to near-CTA size and placed in a random left/right zigzag, so they compete with the RSVP button. 'Saturday 21 June' is centred but the time line under it is left-aligned and squeezed against the left edge. The partner logo placeholder is cut off on the right ('missing asse', 'partner ma') and crammed under the URL, and the can floats in a dead gap while the top half is packed tight.

The two layouts are nearly identical, and they share the same flaws. In both, 'Sunset Sessions' sits almost on the left edge, and the middle column is crammed: the date, the indented '6 pm' line, the pills, the oversized RSVP button and unreadably small legal text are stacked tightly with uneven left edges. The phone also overlaps the placeholder graphic on the right. A wins narrowly because its three pills are compact and evenly spaced. In B the pills are flatter and spread unevenly, the 'Tastings' pill drifts towards the phone, and its pill labels look squeezed.

Both candidates have the same problems. The italic subtitle is jammed right up against the left-aligned 'Saturday 21 June' block, which also clashes with the centred headline. The 'Reserve a spot' line sits right next to the grey placeholder box, so they look crowded together. A is worse in two ways: the TASTINGS pill is pushed right with a bigger gap than the other pills, so the spacing is uneven, and the Reserve line is crammed against the legal text with the phone drifting toward the right edge. B keeps the pills evenly spaced, centres the phone better and leaves room between the Reserve line and the footer.

The two are almost identical, and both share the same flaws. The Inkwell & Lantern logo has shrunk to an unreadable stamp jammed into the card's top-left corner, so the brand is effectively lost. The '24 HOURS' eyebrow sits right of the headline's centre axis, so the two don't align. The fine print is tiny and floats beside the CTA, and the card has a dead band at the bottom. B wins only marginally: its body copy wraps more evenly ('stay as / long as you like') than A's ragged 'stay / as long as', and its book sits slightly higher, leaving more room above the card.

The two candidates are nearly pixel-identical 320x50 banners, so neither is the better resize. Both wrap the headline onto two lines, leaving 'fizz' as an orphan. Both shrink the SOLSTICE can to a tiny, unrecognisable icon jammed under the logo. Both cram the legal line into an illegible block of a few pixels under the CTA. The background circles are reduced to clipped fragments. The CTA is readable and the left-to-right order holds, but the headline wrap and the unreadable legal text are shipping blockers in both.

The two are almost the same layout, and both have the same problems. The GLACIER wordmark floats on its own to the right of the circle. A large empty area sits beside the product, and the left edges don't line up: the headline and body copy start at about x=254, the badges at about 303–310, and the CTA at about 373. The result is a ragged staircase that pushes the CTA off-axis instead of a clean column. A spaces the copy, badges and CTA more evenly. B squeezes the body copy against the badges and leaves a larger empty band at the bottom, so A edges it slightly.

Both put the phone, headline, badges and CTA in a left-to-right row, and in both the CTA is the same size as the badges and the phone runs nearly edge to edge. They also leave SOLSTICE floating above and left of the headline instead of aligned with it. A leaves a big dead gap between the phone and the text, then crams the text, badges and CTA together on the right, and the tagline is tiny. B spreads the elements more evenly across the banner, but its SUMMER ONLY badge sits off on its own, vertically centred and away from its paired badge, which weakens the grouping.

Both are the centred stack shrunk into a wide banner instead of a left-to-right layout. That leaves large empty side areas while the headline, subline and button are squeezed between the top and bottom edges, and the CTA sits very close to the bottom. A's headline is slightly smaller, so the subline has a little room to breathe. B's larger headline pushes 'Now in four flavours.' right up against the line above it, the top margin is thinner, and the vertical spacing is crowded and uneven.

A: the 'WEEKEND ONLY' kicker is cut off from the headline and floats over the button. The can is shrunk to an unrecognisable sliver, and the three-line body copy and legal text are both tiny. Still, the spacing is consistent and nothing collides. B has the same problems, and its 'Shop Sale' button sits right against the 'Ends Sunday' legal block, which leaves the right side cramped and looks like a collision. Its kicker also crowds the top edge of the button, so A is the less bad resize.

The two candidates look the same apart from a 1–2 px horizontal shift. Both have the same flaws. The lilac circle has moved off the product and now sits behind the headline, so 'WEEKEND ONLY' and '20% off' run across its edge. '20% off' nearly touches the right edge of the canvas. The Shop Sale button is jammed right under the subhead, leaving a large empty gap above a small product. The footer line is centred while the top text block is left-aligned.

A works as a left-to-right banner, but the subhead breaks into an awkward three-line stack ('Every / mixed / case.'). The product is tiny inside its circle, the fine print is jammed against the circle, and there is a dead strip on the far right. B is worse: 'off' nearly touches the 'Every mixed case' subhead, which looks like a collision. Its circle is clipped at the top and bottom, the can runs off the bottom edge, and the fine print floats far away on the right with no connection to the rest.

A breaks the subhead as 'Every / mixed case.', which reads cleanly, and spaces the stack fairly evenly. However, the CTA sits far below the subhead, and the product/circle group ends up crowded against the footer text. B has the same structure, but its subhead wrap leaves 'case.' alone on the second line. The product is also pulled up against the CTA, leaving a large empty gap above the footer, so the vertical rhythm is lopsided. In both, the circle is just an arbitrary blob behind the can rather than a deliberate crop as in the original, and the button runs almost to the edges of the canvas.

A and B are almost pixel-identical; the only difference is that B's NEW and Try It pills sit about 5px lower. Both share the same flaws: the bottle cap touches the top edge and the cream circle is jammed into the top-left corner over a stray half-off-canvas ghost circle. The NEW badge is nearly as large as the Try It CTA and competes with it. The right-aligned buttons share no edge with the left-aligned headline, which leaves a dead bottom-left quadrant.

The two candidates are almost identical. Both stack the headline, then the phone in its circle, then the badge, then the CTA. Both share the same flaws: the tilted 'ONLINE ONLY' badge and the 'Try It' button push against the right edge and are uncomfortably tight there, and the supporting copy has dropped below the CTA, which breaks the reading order. The phone and circle sit a few pixels lower in B, and that makes no meaningful difference.

A and B look identical as far as I can see. Both have the same problems. The three tag pills are blown up into big zig-zagging bars that compete with the RSVP button. The date line is centred, but the time and location text under it is left-aligned and ragged. The headline block is crammed under the logo while there is empty space around the product card. The partner placeholder in the bottom right is clipped and overlaps the URL area.

The two are almost identical. Both crowd the middle column: the date, venue, pills, RSVP button, URL and fine print are stacked tightly with almost no gaps, and the legal text is unreadably small. In both, 'Sunset Sessions' runs almost to the left edge of the canvas and across the edge of the circle, '6 pm' is indented out of line with 'Saturday 21 June', and the QR placeholder is jammed against the phone at the right edge. A spreads its three pills wider than the button with large uneven gaps, so they look scattered; B keeps them as one tight group, which makes it slightly less bad.

Both reflow the same way. In both, the 'Live music' tagline is jammed against the left-aligned 'Saturday 21 June' block, which clashes with the centred header. The phone floats off-axis and leaves dead space on the left above the CTA, and the QR placeholder sits next to the URL line. B is worse: the pill gaps are uneven (TASTINGS is pushed right, away from ALL AGES), the phone is shoved toward the right edge, and the URL line and QR box drop down almost onto the legal text, so the bottom looks cramped. A keeps even pill spacing and more breathing room above the fine print.

The two candidates are almost identical. In both, the Inkwell & Lantern logo has shrunk to an illegible thumbnail in the card's top-left corner, the brand's prominence is lost, and the kicker sits off-centre to make room for it. The fine print floats beside the CTA as a separate third column, and the bottom of the card is left empty. The only differences are the body-copy line breaks (A: 'stay as / long as… Tea and'; B: 'stay / as long… Tea / and') and the book sitting slightly lower in B. Neither difference makes one candidate better than the other.
